title: Answers soon in local police shootings
article: Answers are coming soon about Cowichan's two unresolved police shootings.
It's been more than a year since Derek Welton was shot dead by local police, and nine months since Bill Gillespie was wounded.
But investigations into both matters will likely wrap up soon, said Island District RCMP Cpl. Darren Lagan.
"Gillespie's (case) remains with the use-of-force expert, that's the stage the investigation is at," he confirmed.

"In Welton's, we recently received the use-of-force report back, so the (investigation team) is reviewing that and making its final assessment as to whether the package goes to Crown counsel or what the next step will be."
In both cases investigation is conducted by Vancouver Island Integrated Major Crime Unit, led by the Victoria Police Department.
The use-of-force expert is an officer from a municipal police force in B.C. and because of the rarity of these experts, this stage of the investigation is where delays commonly occur.

"They look at the entire investigation and determine the appropriate use of force in that situation, and then they'll determine if the use of force was in keeping with the law first of all, and then the RCMP's policy for use of force," Lagan explained.

"That can be a delay for (the investigation) because it's a very specialized skill -- it's not like every detachment has (a use-of-force expert). It can take several months, if not longer, for (the expert) to get to the file and complete the analysis."
Lagan said parallel to that analysis is a review by Crown counsel, which looks at the entire investigation package and determines if any criminal act was done by the police officer involved.
This Crown analysis usually requires the use-of-force expert as well.
Bill Gillespie admits he's frustrated the process has taken so long.
He was interviewed for the investigation three weeks ago, he said, adding he's ready to apply through the courts for a look at the investigation.
"They haven't told me squat," he said, adding the ordeal has left him in constant, "excruciating pain."
He's being represented by lawyer James Legh and is ready to fight a legal battle to get information.

"I don't know if I'll have access to that report -- they're not doing it up for me, they're doing it for themselves," he fumed. "I told them my side of the story but they won't tell me what happened in the investigation."
But Chris Considine, a Victoria-based lawyer, said these investigations typically take six months to a year or longer depending on circumstances.
"The investigation may take a number of different twists and turns because each case is individual," he said.
Considine said investigators typically review radio transmissions leading up to the encounter as well as any video surveillance from nearby where the shooting happened.
They also interview all involved as well as the victim's family members, friends, physicians, etc, and request medical records, the autopsy report if applicable and toxicology results.
This all takes time, Considine pointed out.

"Usually the results are released to the public and usually before then to the family so the family is kept informed of what's taken place," he added. "My experience is the police are usually very aware of keeping the family informed."

In the meantime, Lagan confirmed the police officer who shot Gillespie is still working but has been assigned to administrative duties, while the officer involved in the Welton incident has returned to active duty.
Derek Welton: Derek Welton died March 1, 2009 after police responded to a call at the Duncan RV Park on Boys Road.
They encountered Welton, a 39-year-old with a long history of violence, who at some point became armed with a knife.
Police said they utilized multiple force options including the use of a Taser, without success. A senior officer with 11 years on the job fired his gun and hit Welton.
An unnamed police officer at the time said it was a "by the book" shooting.

Bill Gillespie: Bill Gillespie was shot Sept. 18, 2009 after police tried to pull him over but he failed to stop, instead driving a couple of blocks to his passenger's driveway on Henry Road in Chemainus.
Gillespie was ordered from the vehicle but reports of what happened after that varies. What's known for sure is Gillespie was shot once in the upper body.
Gillespie, who was "very well known" to police before the incident, said he was complying with police commands when he was shot.
"It was either an accident or he did it with malice, he shot me on purpose," Gillespie reasoned. "I was laying down on the ground doing what they were saying to do."
Police cannot comment on the incident until the investigation is finished.
